messages.subject: distribution modelling-climatic suitability prediction
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm new to NicheMapR. I was thinking of modeling the potential distribution of the pasture mealybug (Heliococcus summervillei) using NicheMapR or modeling/analyzing the climatic suitability and identify seasonal activity patterns in a single location where mealybug has been recorded before, or a far-away independent location where it is not recorded and examining the feasibility of its survival over there.

The study on climatic requirements, biology, and other physiological parameters has not been done before. So, I was wondering if I could use Microclimate, or the Ectotherm model, either separately or together, to develop a model/do an analysis without having lab and field data. Also, if there is any other better way/ideas/function using which I could develop a distribution pattern, or identify how the mealybug interacts at a given location, climate.

Thank you.


regards,
Parbati Ghising

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: distribution modelling-climatic suitability prediction
parts:
Hi Parbati,
Welcome to the group. You really do need some data on the species to do something useful with NicheMapR. The value of a 'mechanistic niche modelling' approach to understanding species' environmental limits is that you can link what you know about the organism's traits. For example, you can compute how its rates (growth, development, movement, reproduction) respond to its body temperature, or how fast it looses water given its cuticle's resistance, etc. because the package allows you to incorporate its microclimatic conditions and behaviour to determine the environments it experiences and how that translates into body temperature and evaporation. Best thing is to look at published studies using the package to get a sense of what's involved. It takes a while to learn the background ideas behind the models to be able to apply them usefully.
Hope that helps,
All the best,
Mike
